model_output.verdict: Your product design work at Loop Fitness is easy to spot, but I’d hesitate to move the resume forward without knowing more about the decisions behind it. I’d also want to know what you’ve been working on in design since leaving Loop.
write_up: You’re a product designer who worked on client sites and apps at Brightpath Studio, then on Loop Fitness’s mobile apps, and you’re now a barista at Ferry Street Coffee. It’s common to see a resume name the work without showing the decisions behind it. For product design, that makes it harder to stand out against resumes that show what a design addressed or changed.

The line about creating Loop’s first design system in Figma is your best model: it names what you made, where it was used and the tool. Your current role accounts for the time after Loop, but your resume doesn’t show whether you’ve done design work since then.

Let’s start with the Loop booking flow and weekly releases. Add the design problem and your contribution where you can, then show what you learned from member tests. If you have recent design projects, your portfolio and resume can show that work too.
